     Squirting Cucumber. Cucurbitaceæ.

     An annual resembling the common watermelon ; herbaceous stems with rough hairs, trail upon the ground, or climb ; flowers yellow ; fruit globular, of the size of a small orange, yellow and smooth when ripe, containing within a hard coriaceous rind, a white, spongy, medullary matter, enclosing numerous ovale, compressed, white or brownish seeds. The plant is a native of Turkey, and abounds in the islands of the Archipelago. It grows also in various parts of Africa and Asia. --Hom. Pharmacopœia.

     Proved by Hahnemann, Ægidi, Stapf, Rückert, Austrian provers and others. See Encyclopædia, vol. 3, p. 477.
